t.1.183.2: But the foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis, together with Rauhiṇeya, suspecting that they were the foremost heroes of the Kurus, went to that workshop of the Bhārgava where those foremost of men were sitting.
t.1.183.1: Having carefully considered those words of their eldest brother, all the sons of Pāṇḍu then sat there, pondering that very matter in their minds; and then, there, the one of immeasurable might…
t.1.183.4: Then Vāsudeva approached the son of Kuntī, the most excellent of the upholders of dharma, and, pressing the feet of King Yudhiṣṭhira the Ājamīḍha, said, "I am Kṛṣṇa."
t.1.183.3: There Kṛṣṇa, together with Rauhiṇeya, saw Ajātaśatru, broad- and long-armed, seated, and the others, radiant as blazing fire, sitting close around him.
t.1.183.6: And Ajātaśatru, the foremost hero of the Kurus, having inquired after his welfare, asked Kṛṣṇa: "How, O Vāsudeva, have all of us, living here in disguise, been recognized by you?"
t.1.183.5: Likewise, following him, Rauhiṇeya did the same, and the delighted Kurus welcomed them both. Then the two heroes of the Yadus clasped the feet of their father's sister, foremost lady of the Bhāratas.
t.1.183.7: Vāsudeva, laughing, said to him: "Even when hidden, fire is surely recognized, O king. Apart from the Pāṇḍavas, what other man among mortals is there who could perform that feat of valor?"
t.1.183.9: "May good fortune be yours; grow strong like a fire being kindled, you who have lain hidden as in a cave. Let none of the kings here come to know of you; for now, we two shall go back to our camp." Then he of imperishable splendor, given leave by the Pāṇḍava, departed swiftly together with Baladeva.
t.1.183.8: By good fortune all of you Pāṇḍavas, vanquishers of foes, have escaped from that fire; by good fortune the wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with his ministers, did not get what he desired.
